newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mostly lower,but off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mostly lower,but off day's lows.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly lower, but drifted above daily lows as funds and dealers took profits on dollar positions, traders and analysts said.
"Anyone who held dollar positions overnight had a nice profit," one currency trader said. "And you saw some new (dollar) shorts established."

He said June marks would continue their downtrend, and that the contract's pop towards $0.5880, or 1.7090 spot, was anticipated. June yen bounced through $0.008012 around midday, as dollar/yen dipped slightly below 126.00 spot.
"The dollar is taking a breather," one futures floor source said.
Pat Donahue, head of Chicago's foreign exchange at NationsBank, looks for the dollar to push higher overnight. He expects the dollar/mark to rise to 1.7230 spot and dollar/yen to hit 127.50 spot.
A rise to those levels would push both June marks and June yen to fresh contract lows at $0.5832 and $0.007924, respectively.
Talk that the Bundesbank sold 10-year U.S. notes raised concerns about central bank dollar selling, and kept key currencies from falling early in the session.

In fact, most contracts gravitated to the upside, with June Swiss francs testing resistance at $0.6859, which roughly corresponded to 1.4687 spot, and June marks meandering to $0.5879 in extremely light trade.
"Sure there are concerns about intervention, but I don't believe Japan and Germany will get serious about intervention at these levels," Donahue said.
He said verbal bashing of the dollar would likely occur once dollar/mark hits 1.75 spot and dollar/yen rallies to 130.00. Those levels correspond to $0.5734 in June marks and $0.007773 in June yen.
Many futures traders believe those downward targets in June yen and marks will be hit within the month.

June Mexican pesos tested a key retracement level at $0.123000. One floor trader said 400 contracts traded at that level, which represents an upward retracement from the contract's decline in February. He pegged resistance at $0.123200 to $0.123600.

At the end of pit trade, June yen lost $0.000044 at $0.008003, marks were off $0.0014 at $0.5862, Swiss francs were down $0.0022 at $0.6841, sterling was down $0.0018 at $1.6250, Canadian dollars were off $0.0007 at $0.7237, Aussie dollars were up $0.0051 at $0.7804 and pesos were up $0.000125 at $0.122700.
